agreements.statement: Both participants converge on the same root cause (H1): a case-sensitive card-type comparison in validateCard at src/payment/card.js line 12 rejects the lowercase 'visa' card type because only 'VISA' or 'MasterCard' are accepted. The trace (card_type 'visa', card_valid:true, STATUS_CODE_ERROR) and log ('cannot process visa credit cards. Only VISA or MasterCard') are mutually consistent tokens of the same deterministic validation rejection.

Both agree the failure is introduced/latent to the S2 deployment: the error metric is 0 in the window ending at the S2 deployment (sha256:29ccc4ff...) and becomes 1 after (sha256:1a39d536...), and the deployment event (sha256:999345e8...) pins before/after versions (c1c9fbcc -> bb66d2da) at 2026-08-16T16:58:19.886Z.

Both treat the paymentUnreachable=true flag (sha256:596fa121...) as non-causal context: the failing charge span executes inside the payment service and emits a semantic card-type error, not an unreachability/connectivity condition.
Both correctly note paymentFailure=0 (sha256:2ff58ad6...) rules out a deliberate payment-failure chaos injection as the trigger.

Both participants' proposed remediation converges on normalizing card-type casing in validateCard and/or rolling back to before_version c1c9fbcc...; both frame flag toggles as discriminating tests rather than the fix.

contradictions.statement: No substantive contradiction between participants. The only divergence is marginal: p-1 retains H2 (paymentUnreachable flag) as a 'proposed' open alternative that it itself largely refutes via its own objection and predicts will still fail when toggled, whereas p-2 explicitly marks H2 as 'rejected'. This is a status/positioning difference, not a causal disagreement.

blind_spots.statement: Neither participant reconciles the apparent tension between 'every valid charge fails' (incident wording) and the sampled/aggregated evidence showing only 1 error call at ~4 calls/sec with coverage_verified only on the pre-deployment window; the post-deployment metric lacks coverage_verified/backend_health, so the extrapolation from 1 observed error to 'every charge fails' is asserted, not evidenced.

Neither participant explains why the trace's card_type is lowercase 'visa' when the incident is described as 'every valid charge' — i.e., whether the charge driver always emits lowercase types (making it universal) or whether only some cards are lowercase (making 'every' an overstatement).

Neither participant addresses service topology (checkout -> payment gRPC) or whether the observed charge driver traffic (4 req/s) is representative of storefront traffic, which the Context Brief flags as a known limit.

No participant proposes verifying the exact S2 diff (diff_hash sha256:095af597...) to confirm validateCard was actually modified in S2, rather than merely existing; the code-location evidence is keyed to commit S2 but a before/after comparison is absent.

Neither participant grounds the regime before S2: the pre-deployment metric (sha256:29ccc4ff...) shows 0 errors at 7.88 calls/sec, but no positive 'charges succeeded' evidence confirms the service worked correctly pre-deployment.

unique_findings.statement: p-1 (code-defect-hunter) is the only participant to explicitly invoke the paymentFailure=0 flag in its stated objections as an exclusion of a chaos-injection cause and to propose a discriminating test (t2) that toggles the flag while holding the lowercase 'visa' card fixed to prove the flag is not the root cause.

p-1 is the only participant to expose the literal contradiction inside the log/error text (accepted set is literally 'VISA' or 'MasterCard' vs. incoming 'visa') as the direct mechanism, and to cite the opposing-flag evidence item explicitly in its support/opposition structure.

p-2 (system-level-causation) is the only participant to frame refutation at the system level: the charge span executing to completion inside the payment service demonstrates service reachability, which disqualifies the paymentUnreachable flag hypothesis more rigorously than p-1's weaker positional objection.

p-2 uniquely surfaces the rollback hypothesis as a first-class predicted observation / proposed test (deploy before_version c1c9fbcc... and observe the error metric drop to 0), which is the cleanest falsifiable confirmation of the S2-localized root cause.
